sheet-1-1.description: The main map of sheet 1, drawn at 100 feet to an inch in the lower left of the title sheet below the key map, covers the eastern side of Blackwood village from Church Street south to beyond Lake Avenue, between Main Street or Black Horse Pike on the west and the vacant land east of Ohio Avenue. New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Ohio Avenues run north and south across it, laid out in long narrow lots with alternate street numbers; most blocks are vacant or carry only scattered frame dwellings with sheds, garages and stables. The north side of Church Street is the most built up: the Blackwood M.E. Church and the M.E. Church Cemetery, a row of dwellings, and the Blackwood Public School. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are shown along Church Street, New Jersey Avenue and Ohio Avenue, with fire hydrants at the corners. In the lower left the Black Horse Pike crosses Lake Avenue diagonally, with a few dwellings in blocks 34 and 43. Blocks 44, 45 and 46 south of Lake Avenue are almost empty, and the land east of Ohio Avenue and north of the church row is marked vacant beyond. The part is drawn with north straight up the page, unlike sheets 2 to 4, whose streets run at about 20 degrees to the page. A heavy line separates it from the key map above and from the Camden County Farms part to the right, which lies about a mile south of the village.
notes: Church is today East Church Street; Lake Avenue is East Lake Avenue; Pennsylvania Avenue is North Pennsylvania Avenue north of Church and South Pennsylvania Avenue south of it; Main Street or Black Horse Pike is Black Horse Pike.
At New Jersey Avenue, Lake Avenue jogs: the leg west to the Black Horse Pike is drawn diagonally and about 40 ft south of the leg to the east.
Buildings of note: Blackwood M.E. Church, Blackwood Public School.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, shows the business centre of Blackwood around the crossing of Church Street with Main Street or Black Horse Pike, from Harrison Avenue east to beyond the Pike and from the lots north of Church Street south to Lake Avenue. Elm Avenue and Central Avenue divide the residential blocks west of the Pike into long narrow lots of frame dwellings, most with sheds, stables or garages behind. Commercial buildings line the west side of the Pike: the Blackwood Auto Paint Co., the Blackwood Theatre (motion pictures, concrete block), the South Jersey Bank, and the Blackwood Fire Co. fire department building on Central Avenue. On the east side of the Pike stand the First National Bank, a bakery, a blacksmith shop, a carpenter's shop and a garage for fifteen cars, with stores and dwellings between. The Blackwood Grange hall stands north of Church Street near Harrison Avenue. In the north-east corner are the Blackwood Cemetery and the First Presbyterian Church, facing Church Street where it angles away to the south-east from the Pike. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run along Church Street, Central Avenue, Lake Avenue and the Pike, with fire hydrants at most corners. New Jersey Avenue enters in the extreme south-east corner. The sheet is drawn with the street grid turned about 20 degrees to the page; its neighbours are sheet 3 to the north, sheet 4 to the west and sheet 1 to the east and south.
notes: Church is today West Church Street west of the Pike and East Church Street east of it; Central Avenue is West Central Avenue; Lake Avenue is West Lake Avenue; Main Street or Black Horse Pike is Black Horse Pike.
East Church Street leaves the Pike about 30 ft south of West Church Street, as drawn.
Buildings of note: Blackwood Grange, First National Bank, South Jersey Bank, Blackwood Theatre, Blackwood Fire Co., First Presbyterian Church, Blackwood Auto Paint Co.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the northern part of Blackwood village between Harrison Avenue on the west and Main Street or Black Horse Pike, with a strip of lots east of the Pike. Prospect, Lincoln, Garfield and Cleveland Avenues run east and west across it, dividing blocks 23, 25 and 28, which are laid out in long narrow lots and only partly built up with frame dwellings, garages, sheds, hen houses and a wagon house. Along the east side of the Pike, in block 26, stand a row of dwellings with stables and storage sheds. North of Prospect Avenue the land is largely open (block 22), with the Blackwood Water Co.'s 40,000 gallon water tank on a steel tower in the north-west corner, and the Pike curving away to the north-east. The post office stands on the Pike at the south edge of the sheet. Six-inch water pipes run along Prospect Avenue, Garfield Avenue, Harrison Avenue and the Pike, with fire hydrants at the corners. Harrison Avenue is drawn along the western edge with only its east side complete. The street grid is turned about 19 degrees to the page. Sheet 4 adjoins on the west and sheet 2 on the south.
notes: Main Street or Black Horse Pike is today Black Horse Pike; the other streets keep their names.
North of Prospect Avenue the Pike is drawn curving to the north-east; today's Black Horse Pike runs straight north.
Harrison Avenue junctions were placed by hand, half the labelled 50 ft width from the drawn east edge; the detector paired the east edge with lot lines.

map; 50 ft to an inch. North of the centre: Prospect, Lincoln, Garfield and Cleveland Avs. between Harrison Av. and Main St. or Black Horse Pike; Blackwood Water Co. tank. The Harrison Av. junctions were hand-picked (east edge minus 25 ft): the detector paired the drawn edge with lot lines 40 to 65 ft inside the blocks and the scale came out 4 percent low.
streetnames: Main Street or Black Horse Pike

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the western side of Blackwood: the Lake Morgan dam and mill site, the railroad corridor, and the Blackwood Crest development. In the north-west, Collins Landing or Good Intent Road and Barnesboro Road meet at the head of Lake Morgan, where the old mill building houses the Blackwood Water Co. pumping station beside the tail race of Timber Creek; Bull Run enters from the north-west and Lake Drive follows the lake shore. Glen, Rossiter and Beaver are platted but marked not open. The Philadelphia and Reading Railroad (Grenloch Branch) runs through the middle of the sheet with the passenger depot and a freight depot, flanked to the south by West and East Railroad Avenues. Nearby are the Community Masonic Club, the Lakeside Hotel, the Denver House, the E. Frank Pine lumber and builders' supplies yard with a woodworking shop, and a hosiery factory not in operation. At the south-east corner stands the Welsbach Co. (Blackwood Foundry Co.) foundry. North of Church, between Church Street Court and Harrison Avenue, lie residential blocks on Lincoln, Garfield and Cleveland Avenues. South-west of the railroad, Blackwood Crest is laid out in narrow lots along Central and Clifton Avenues and the loop of Lake Avenue around the lake shore, with A Court and, across the water, Morgan Place. The street grid is turned about 17 degrees to the page.
notes: Church Street Court is today Baptist Lane; Church is West Church Street; Central Avenue is West Central Avenue; the Lake Avenue loop around Blackwood Crest is Lakeside Avenue; Barnesboro Road is Blackwood-Barnsboro Road.
Collins Landing or Good Intent Road: the north leg is today Good Intent Road; the leg south-east across the dam is part of West Church Street.
The railroad bed north of Church is today Washington Avenue; no railroad remains in OpenStreetMap here.
Church on this sheet is drawn about 6 m out of place relative to Cleveland Avenue; its junctions were left out of the fit.
Glen, Rossiter and Beaver are marked not open.
